title: Pool chemicals: types, hazards and safe handling
audience: Pool service technicians who receive, store, handle or add pool chemicals
learningOutcomes: Name the main pool chemical types listed in the textbook and state what each is used for
Explain the hazards of each type and why incompatible products must be kept apart
Read the safety data sheet for a pool chemical before it is handled, and follow its protective requirements
Apply the extra care the textbook requires for small pools and baby pools

instruction.heading: The chemical types in the textbook
instruction.body: The textbook lists several products used to clean and treat pool water: granular or tablet forms of a chlorine donor, namely trichloroisocyanuric acid and sodium dichloroisocyanurate, which dissolves quickly; hydrochloric acid, liquid chlorine, and an alum-based clarifier. Chlorine donors kill bacteria and algae. Acids lower pH and clean surfaces. Alum is a clarifier that makes fine particles clump so the filter can catch them. The textbook gives a chlorine content for one of the products. Each product has its own hazards, and its safety data sheet is the reference.

instruction.heading: Hazards and separation
instruction.body: The products listed in the textbook are hazardous and must not be mixed. Chlorine donors and acids are incompatible, and combining them can release a toxic gas. The handbook and the textbook both stress keeping products apart and never moving one product into another's container. The separation rules are described in “Pool chemical handling and storage at home”, and the chemistry rules in “Disinfection chemistry and pH interpretation”. Storage must be cool, dry, ventilated, lockable, and kept away from the filter together with the pump.

instruction.heading: Reading the safety data sheet
instruction.body: Read the safety data sheet for each product before handling it. It gives the hazards, the protective equipment, first aid, storage and disposal. Keep the sheet where it is reachable found on site. The textbook does not replace the sheet, and where any protective advice in this lesson differs from the sheet, the sheet governs.

instruction.heading: Small pools and baby pools
instruction.body: The textbook warns that extra care is needed when cleaning baby pools with these products. A small amount of water changes concentration quickly, so a little product can produce a high level in the water. Use a reduced dose only where the plan allows one, keep children well away, and record the product, the amount and the time. If the plan does not cover the small pool, refer the question to the operator.

instruction.heading: What this lesson does not authorise
instruction.body: This lesson grants no licence or permit to handle, store or carry dangerous goods, and it does not replace the operator's instruction or the safety data sheet.

procedure: Identify the product and read its label and safety data sheet before opening it.
Put on the protective equipment named in the safety data sheet.
Confirm the product is not going into a container for another product, and not mixed with any other product.
Dissolve and add the product as “Pool chemical handling and storage at home” describes, and in the order the plan gives.
For a small pool, confirm the plan allows the dose and keep children away.
Return the product to its own labelled container, and store it separately and locked.
Record the product, amount, time and storage check.

workedExamples.situation: A baby pool needs cleaning and the owner says to use the same dose as the full-size pool.
workedExamples.reasoning: Avoid using the full-size dose. The textbook warns of extra care in small pools. Check the plan for the small-pool dose, keep children away, and record the product and amount. If the plan does not cover the small pool, refer the question to the operator.

workedExamples.situation: A supplier delivers an acid and a chlorine product in the same box, with no separation.
workedExamples.reasoning: Separate them at once and store them apart, in their own labelled containers. Read each safety data sheet, record the delivery, and tell the supplier. Do not mix them to make room.

equipmentAndPpe: Safety data sheet for each product
Protective gloves, eye protection and any respiratory protection named in the sheet
Labelled bucket and paddle for each product
Lockable, ventilated storage with separation by type
Record sheet for product, amount and storage

commonErrors.error: Storing acids and chlorine products together
commonErrors.prevention: Store each type separately, locked and away from the filter.

commonErrors.error: Using the full pool dose in a small pool
commonErrors.prevention: Use only the small-pool dose the plan allows, and refer any gap.

commonErrors.error: Handling a product without reading its data sheet
commonErrors.prevention: Read the sheet before opening the product.

commonErrors.error: Leaving a product with a loose cap or in an unlabelled container
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the original label and cap, and report any leaking container.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Pool chemicals are hazardous. Incompatible products, such as acids and chlorine donors, must be kept apart, and mixing them can release toxic gas.
Extra care is needed when cleaning baby pools and small pools with these cleaners. Keep children away from the chemicals and the water during treatment.
Never let children handle pool chemicals.
Read the safety data sheet before handling any product, and follow the protective equipment it names.
Storage and handling of pool chemicals in quantity are subject to dangerous goods and work health and safety rules, so check with the relevant regulator before relying on this point.
This lesson grants no licence or permit to handle, store, transport or treat water with dangerous goods.

qualityStandard: Every product is handled with its safety data sheet read and the named protective equipment worn.
Incompatible products are stored apart and are never mixed.
Small-pool treatment uses only the plan's small-pool dose, with children kept away.
documentationEvidence: Product use record with amount, time and dose basis
Referral note for unclear small-pool or storage questions
summary: Each chemical has its own hazard. The safety data sheet is the reference.
Keep incompatible products apart and never mix them.
Small pools need extra care, and children must be kept away from the chemicals.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must acids and chlorine donors be stored apart?
options: Because the textbook says they must be kept in the same place
Because they look similar on the shelf and the labels are small
Because mixing incompatible products can release toxic gas
Because storage space is limited and the shelf is high

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the textbook say about cleaning a baby pool with pool cleaners?
options: Mix the cleaners with bleach to make them stronger
Let children help to add the product and watch the dose carefully
Use the full-size dose to be safe in every pool and every tub
Take extra care, and use a dose only where the plan allows

knowledgeChecks.question: Before a pool chemical is handled, what should be read first?
options: The safety data sheet and the product label
The brand advertising on the packaging
The owner's notes from the last visit
